claim: Recomputing checkpoint PD from fresh native-model state at 2 kHz did not revive sustained turning in the matched delayed-command diagnostic.

harness.model: vendored native MJCF with qualification floor; common backend mirrors its joint losses
harness.startup: zero command through 1 s, StartupSettle 1-3 s, +0.3 rad/s from 3-13 s, zero after
harness.qualification_boundary: headless diagnostic only; not a common ROS launch or hardware result

interpretation: Fresh 2 kHz PD changes early yaw and produces a small late-yaw difference, but both modes collapse to the same parked-policy effort level. This refutes intra-interval PD refresh alone as the stall remedy for this matched native-model diagnostic.
limitations: The native MJCF diagnostic is not the full common ROS graph and does not include GUI/twist_mux behavior.
No contact-fidelity A/B or target-domain retraining was attempted.
The result is a negative diagnostic, not a claim that all high-rate control implementations are equivalent.
